thread:
Alex P: FYI getting a support escalation — customer A sees a bunch of 429/503 bursts for /v1/generate even though their quota shows tokens left. Happened around 12:03 UTC.
Jordana K: ugh, did they give repro or sample request ids?
Alex P: Support attached a sample request-id header: req_2026_03_12_9c7f. They sent a 5k-token prompt, then a small follow-up.
Support L2: attaching logs we have: 
```
2026-03-12T12:03:02Z req_2026_03_9c7f RATE_LIMIT_BLOCK user=acct_42 route=/v1/generate limiter=global-burst
2026-03-12T12:03:02Z req_2026_03_9c7f RESPONSE 429
2026-03-12T12:03:05Z req_2026_03_9c7f RETRY 503 downstream
```
Samir G: can you paste the limiter config for that account? suspect burst window or refill units mismatch.
Alex P: config snippet from DB (redacted): 
```
{ "bucket": "acct_42", "capacity": 100000, "refill_rate": 3600, "unit": "minute", "burst_window_ms": 200 }
```
Jordana K: refill_rate=3600 + unit=minute looks like it's already tokens/min, but UI shows tokens/sec earlier — maybe a migration mismatch where unit was supposed to be "second". If refill used wrong unit we'd allow 60x fewer tokens.
Samir G: timeline-wise, customer previously had a heavy 5k prompt that consumed a big chunk; then small followups should have been allowed if burst logic allowed prefix caching. Are there any recent deploys to limiter?
ops-bot: deploy/redwood-limiter v3.14 rolled at 2026-03-12T11:58:00Z by jordana.
Jordana K: oh — that deploy included the unit normalization change I pushed. I added a config migration but maybe it skipped accounts created before 2025.
Alex P: quick test: I patched a local limiter with unit="second" and replayed their sequence — no 429s. With unit="minute" I reproduced 429s within ~10s.
Samir G: looks like a config-migration hole + aggressive burst_window_ms. For immediate mitigation: 1) update acct_42 refill unit to second 2) increase burst_window_ms to 2k for a short window 3) rollback the migration in config service?
Jordana K: agree. I'll push a hotfix to the migration script to re-run for accounts < created_at 2025-01-01. Also schedule a config reload for acct_42.
Support L2: communicated to customer: "we found a config mismatch causing lower refill than expected — applying fix now and will monitor for 15m" :thumbsup:
Alex P: ops, please run this db update for the one-off while migration fix lands: 
```
UPDATE limiter_configs SET unit='second' WHERE account_id='acct_42' AND unit='minute';
```
Samir G: after we patch, add an automated smoke-check: send two small back-to-back requests and assert 200. I'll add a runbook step.
Jordana K: deploying migration patch now (canary 5% -> 50% -> 100%). I'll watch telemetry.
ops-bot: canary rollout started for limiter-migration-patch by jordana.
Alex P: postmortem notes we should add: - add config-version tag to each limiter config - expose effective "refill/sec" in console - alert when refill unit ambiguous for accounts older than migration cutoff - add canary guard to prevent migration skipping records
Support L2: customer confirmed reduced errors after ~3 minutes.
Samir G: leaving followups: (1) migration re-run ticket (#INC-4521) assigned to Jordana (2) add smoke test to infra-tests (3) add dashboard panel for refill/sec anomalies.
Jordana K: will file INC-4521 and put ETA EOD. Thanks y'all.
Alex P: nice recovery. please add blameless postmortem and mark status resolved once migration completes. :white_check_mark:
